description:
FILED s523 (Fable, 2026-10-20 22:2x) from the ROUND-3 board (MAIN-READY-38): Scalar-List-Utils t/exotic_names.t moved from a `*FILE*` row (`XSLoader::load() with no args`, NS:DynaLoader) to PARTIAL 652/908 of 1,560 -- it runs on aff112d7 too (pre-s521e; one-file runs on the base-aff112d7 and base-8038fac6 extractions = 652/908 each), so the load fix landed between MAIN-READY-34 (round 2: FAIL 0/0) and -36 (s521c / s521d: #3492 gave every anon sub a home package through sb-int:named-lambda, lib/B.pm's export list #3514 -- one of those made `require Sub::Util` succeed).  THE 908 ROWS are four descriptions x 227 exotic names (\x00..\xff etc.): `caller() in renamed closure returns correct name when it contains \xNN` (260), `stash name for renamed closure is correct ...` (260), `caller() in natively compiled sub ...` (194), `stash name for natively compiled sub ...` (194).  PROBE (scratchpad subname.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl at a6b2a574): `my $s = set_subname("main::x\x00y", sub { (caller(0))[3] })` -- perl: subname($s) = `main::x` (perl TRUNCATES the name at the NUL in subname's answer? no: it is the stash name up to the NUL as the test expects), $s->() = `main::x\x00y`; PCL: subname = `__ANON__`, $s->() = `` (EMPTY).  The PLAIN name fails the same way: `set_subname("Foo::plain", sub { (caller(0))[3] })` -> perl `Foo::plain / Foo::plain`, PCL `__ANON__ / ` -- so set_subname does nothing in lib/Sub/Util.pm (line 61) and `caller(0)[3]` inside an ANON sub answers empty where perl answers `main::__ANON__`.  TWO mechanisms, same file: (1) the shim's set_subname must RENAME the function (the s521d #3492 named-lambda carries `PKG::__ANON__`; a rename = a new name on that record + subname reading it) and `subname` must read it back; (2) caller(0)[3] for an anon sub = `PKG::__ANON__` (perl) -- today empty; after set_subname = the set name.  The `natively compiled sub` half (string-eval'd `sub NAME {...}` with exotic bytes in NAME, then `(caller(0))[3]` + the stash key) tests the same two answers for a NAMED sub with NUL / control / high bytes in its name.  Rows: bless the 908 with THIS cause (done s523 round 3); acceptance = `tools/run-dist-t.pl --rows --no-dist-lib ~/.cpan/build/Scalar-List-Utils-1.70-0 t/exotic_names.t` 652/908 -> 1560/0; also subname.t (21 rows, ruled XS) may move.  Layer: lib/Sub/Util.pm (the shim) + the runtime's caller(0)[3] for anon subs (cl/, the #3492 record).  Part of #1571's `subname` line (split out as this task).  Batch 6 candidate (small module-surface).

=== DONE (s523b, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-20) -- the NAME half; the caller half is #233's RULED deferral ===
MEASURED (scratch/s523b/p1/anon.pl, perl / base 6cf75804 / tree): TWO mechanisms, as filed.  (1) the shim's set_subname / subname were stubs.  (2) caller(0)[3] inside an anonymous sub: an anonymous sub pushes NO call frame at all (only p-sub's named lambda binds *pcl-caller-subname-stack*), so caller(0) inside it reads the ENCLOSING frame (`sub f { sub { (caller(0))[3] }->() }` = main::f, perl main::__ANON__; caller(1) is shifted too).  That is the documented #233 list ("the package is empty inside an anonymous sub", docs/not-supported.md "caller() fidelity [DEFERRED for now]", USER s488: a priority call, no per-call bookkeeping without a measured reason) -- NOT re-litigated; lifting it is a USER decision (it adds a frame bind to EVERY anonymous-sub call).
FIXED (1): runtime builtin SET_SUB_NAME writes the ONE name record (%pcl-sub-names, the one `sub NAME` writes and builtin::sub_name / B's GV read; perl's set_subname gives the CV a new GV and clears CVf_ANON -- probed).  lib/Sub/Util.pm: set_subname qualifies the name as perl does (no package -> main::, leading :: -> main, ' -> ::) and returns the SAME reference without installing anything; subname reads through B's _name_parts (one reader) and, as perl 5.40.3, stops at a NUL.  lib/B.pm's _name_parts splits at the LAST `::` (a lone `:` is a name byte -- the first version aborted exotic_names.t at \x3A).
GUARD: Pl/t/sub-util-01.t NEW, 12 rows, 11 FAIL on the 6cf75804 extraction (U2 same-ref passes there).
ACCEPTANCE: SLU t/exotic_names.t 652/908 -> 912/648 of 1560 (the 260 "stash name for renamed closure" rows left baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv by edit); the 648 left: 260 "caller() in renamed closure" re-caused NS #233 (no frame for an anonymous sub), 388 "natively compiled sub" re-caused #3670 (stash alias) + #3671 (upper-cased package name) -- both FILED.  t/subname.t 0/0 of 21: it dies in B::Deparse (NS), row re-caused.  Try-Tiny named.t 0/3: the three rows read caller(0)[3] INSIDE the renamed try/catch/finally block = #233, re-caused (finally.t's #1571 row 30 is the DESTROY park's file, untouched).
